name: J. H. Kelly
role: Telegraph operator at Medora, then Dickinson
bio: J. H. Kelly of Duluth took over Medora's telegraph office in September 1884. In November 1884 he moved to the operator's job at Dickinson.

moments.label: Took over the Medora telegraph office

mentions: J. H. Kelly, of Duluth, now manipulates the electric-telegraph apparatus at the telegraph office, Mr. Smith having departed for Illinois.

Changes are coming thick and fast in the railroad employes here. Kelly has gone to Dickinson, and his place has been taken by L. W. Anderson. Ives is in Sentinel Butte, and S. P. Elverson has his place as night operator, and Mr. Maxwell, fo…

…eft us. As a lightning jerker and jolly good fellow he has not a superior on the line. His change, taking Mr. Kelly's place as operator, at Dickinson, is a promotion, but it was as distasteful to him as to the many friends he left behind. Come again, Ole.
